plan.rationale: Initial plan for M=32,N=4096,K=4096. block_M restricted to [16,32] since M=32 must be divisible and larger tiles would waste rows; block_N spans 64..256 to control launch count over the wide N; block_K and stages explore pipeline depth; threads [64,128,256] to probe warp layout given the proxy ties them. swizzle=[0] establishes the required row-major baseline (one tile row makes swizzle launch-equivalent anyway). Shared estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*stages, 4*block_M*block_N) with a 32768-byte cap, well under the portability limit for these small M tiles. Equal weights initially; next hypothesis: after baseline, expand swizzle and test a changed block_K/thread domain to see whether pipeline depth or thread count drives simulated latency, acknowledging this proxy is dimensionless and GB10 estimates are simulator-only.

Second-round plan for M=32,N=4096,K=4096. Attempt-00 (32x64x32,3 stages,256 threads,swizzle 0) passed numerics/compile and simulated at 195.8 us with 18KB smem, 4 blocks/SM, ~33.8 MB simulated DRAM. M=32 keeps block_M in [16,32] (larger tiles waste rows); block_N spans 64..256 to probe launch-count vs traffic trade-off on the wide N; block_K stays [32,64,128]; stages restricted to [2,3,4] since stage 1 rarely helps a K=4096 pipeline; threads narrowed to [128,256] since attempt-00 already used 256 and this tests whether 128 changes simulated latency given the proxy ties them. Per the guidance, swizzle is now expanded to [0,4,8,16,32,64] to test serpentine panel locality; note that with ceil(M/block_M)=1 or 2 tile rows, most swizzles will be launch-equivalent and deduplicated, so the real signal will come from tile/stage/thread changes—next hypothesis is to test whether a changed thread domain (128) or larger block_N with deeper stages lowers simulated latency under the same 32KB cap. Equal weights retained; the panel-reuse feature is an analytic hypothesis, so we will inspect simulated DRAM/latency and revise weights if locality gains do not materialize. GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal checks execute the exact source/TIR but not the CUDA binary.

Third-round plan for M=32,N=4096,K=4096. Both prior attempts passed numerics/compile; attempt-01 (16x64x64,2 stages,256 threads,swizzle 4) improved simulated latency to 176.4 us vs 195.8 us, but simulated DRAM stayed ~33.8 MB, so the panel-reuse hypothesis produced no measured locality gain and swizzles remain largely launch-equivalent with only 1-2 tile rows (ceil(32/16)=2, ceil(32/32)=1). block_M stays [16,32] since larger tiles waste M rows; block_N spans 64..256; block_K [32,64,128]. Threads narrowed to [128] to isolate the thread-count hypothesis the proxy ties: attempt-00 and attempt-01 both used 256, so 128 is an untested branch per the guidance to change thread or block_K domain early. Stages restricted to [2,3,4] as stage 1 rarely helps a K=4096 pipeline. Weights adjusted from equal to emphasize pipeline (1.5) since accumulated DRAM was flat and latency is likely pipeline/occupancy-bound, and de-emphasize footprint (0.5) since smem usage is well under cap; traffic/launches kept at 1.0. Shared estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*stages, 4*block_M*block_N) under the 32768 cap and portability limit. Next hypothesis: with 128 threads, deeper stages and possibly block_N=128/256 may lower simulated latency; if 128 threads regresses, revert to 256. GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal checks validate exact source/TIR but do not execute the CUDA binary.

Fourth-round plan for M=32,N=4096,K=4096. History: attempt-00 195.8us (256thr,3st), attempt-01 176.4us (256thr,2st), attempt-02 147.6us (128thr,3st) — all passed numerics/compile, DRAM flat ~33.8MB so panel locality never materialized; swizzles remain launch-equivalent with ceil(M/block_M) in {1,2}. Threads reduced to 128 improved latency, so we probe 64 threads (untested branch) while keeping 128 as the incumbent; block_M stays [16,32] since larger tiles waste M rows and small M needs blocks for occupancy; block_N spans 64..256 (attempt-02 used 64; worth testing wider N with fewer launches); block_K [32,64,128] kept broad since only 64 has been measured; stages [2,3,4] as stage 1 rarely helps K=4096; swizzle expanded again but expected launch-equivalent. Weights kept from attempt-02 (pipeline 1.5, footprint 0.5) since flat DRAM confirms latency is pipeline/occupancy-bound rather than traffic-bound. Shared estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*stages, 4*block_M*block_N) under 32768 cap and portability limit. Next hypothesis: 64 threads and/or larger block_N with 3-4 stages may reduce simulated latency; if 64-thread regresses revert to 128. GB10 values are simulator-only estimates; Metal checks validate exact source/TIR but do not execute the CUDA binary. No global optimality claimed.
